summary:
Moquegua department stands under Peru's national framework. No Moquegua-specific trans statute, municipal ordinance, court finding or enforcement action appears in the sources; the national rules described below bind the department directly.

Two legislative stages restrict which public restrooms a trans visitor may use. On 20 February 2025 the Congress' Commission on Women and Family unanimously approved a dictamen covering bills 6506 and 8457 that would bar entry to public sanitary facilities designated for the sex other than one's birth sex, with exceptions only for custody, medical care, or accompanying an adult, a child under 12 or a disabled person, and would require unambiguous signage; as of publication the measure still awaited plenary backing. Trans-rights activist Gianna Camacho called it discriminatory, warning that security staff would effectively judge people by personal criteria such as requesting a DNI. The Congress plenary then approved, on 2 April 2025 and exempt from second vote, the dictamen of the law 'fortaleciendo el derecho a la indemnidad sexual de los niños y adolescentes', whose article 5 bars anyone whose biological sex does not match the facility's intended sex from public sanitary facilities, with exceptions limited to accompanying or assisting minors, patients or people with specific needs. IDEHPUCP analysts Miriam Tovar and Gonzalo Ugarte argue the measure implicitly brands trans people as more prone to entering bathrooms to harass or sexually abuse minors, conditions basic rights on verifiable 'biological sex', and violates equality, non-discrimination and gender self-determination; they note Congress had already banned inclusive language and again rejected equal marriage.

Violence against trans people is rising and recorded figures understate it. The TLGBI Rights Observatory's annual report records 54 killings of TLGBI people and 170 rights-violation cases in Peru between 2020 and 2023, with trans women the most affected and hate crimes rising. The report recounts the February 2023 kidnapping of trans woman Rubí Torres Silvano (31) in central Lima and her murder in Carabayllo with approximately 30 gunshots at the hands of the 'Los Gallegos' gang, with bodies showing gunshots, stab wounds and throat-slitting indicating extreme hate. These national figures describe the risk environment applicable to Moquegua.
tangentialFactors:
The restroom restrictions rest on a framing that treats trans people as a risk to children in shared facilities, a framing that IDEHPUCP links to the broader pattern of Congress having already banned inclusive language and repeatedly rejected equal marriage. Security staff and members of the public, not only police, become de facto adjudicators of a visitor's sex under the signage and 'biological sex' requirements, which raises the likelihood of challenge in hotels, restaurants, shopping centres and transport hubs throughout Moquegua.

The recorded national violence figures are drawn from a sub-registry: co-author Gianna Camacho has stated that the recorded numbers undercount actual incidents, so the department's apparent quietness in the sources cannot be read as an absence of risk.
localsOnly: Trans residents of Moquegua face the same national legal position as visitors on restroom access, anti-discrimination coverage and document rules, but also carry the resident-facing burdens the sources record nationally: the absence of statutory hate-crime and anti-discrimination protection, the requirement to litigate gender-marker changes case by case through the judicial process, and exposure to police and public violence documented in the national observatory figures. No Moquegua-specific enforcement pattern, municipal practice or local support organisation appears in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes: No Moquegua-specific trans statute, ordinance, court finding, enforcement action, healthcare practice or incident appears in the source inventory; whether the department's municipal authorities or health facilities apply the national restroom and classification rules in any documented local manner is unresolved and not sourced here. The sources do not record DNI or passport marker practice at Moquegua's entry points or within its territory, and any local pattern of secondary screening or identity challenge is unresolved. The status of the pending Gender Identity Law as it affects residents of Moquegua after the March 2021 reference point is not sourced.
